finding.summary: Truncation cuts the report from the end, but render_report places the '## ⚠️ Not fully reviewed' and '## Excluded from review' disclosures at the tail, while the REVIEW_SIGNATURE and 'Reviewed commit: <sha>' header sit at the top. On a large report (>65,000 chars, plausible on big PRs with many findings), truncation silently deletes exactly the incomplete/excluded disclosures this PR promises to always surface, while the surviving header still carries the signature and head SHA — so the truncated comment becomes the --since-last-review baseline and implies full coverage of files that were never reviewed or were excluded.
finding.fix: Make the disclosure block truncation-proof: either render the signature, reviewed-SHA, and incomplete/excluded sections into a fixed trailer that is appended after truncation (truncating only the overview/issues middle), or cap the number of rendered issues in render_report so the assembled report can never exceed MAX_COMMENT_CHARS, or at minimum append a '… disclosures omitted by truncation' marker whenever truncation occurs so readers know coverage claims are incomplete.

label: false_positive
label_reason: Raised in review and merged with the file unchanged.
